message.content:
I don’t have access to live sensor feeds, so I can’t give you the exact AQI value for Los Angeles at this very moment. However, here’s what you can do to find the current air quality:

| Source | How to Check | Typical Metrics |
|--------|--------------|-----------------|
| **EPA AirNow** (airnow.gov) | Search “Los Angeles” → “Air Quality” → “Current Conditions” | AQI (0‑500), PM₂.₅, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂ |
| **OpenAQ** (openaq.org) | Use the “Locations” tab → filter by city or state | PM₂.₅, PM₁₀, O₃, NO₂, CO, SO₂ |
| **Weather Apps** (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather) | Look for “Air Quality” section | AQI, pollutant concentrations |
| **Local News** (e.g., LA Times, KABC) | Check their “Environment” or “Health” sections | Often report AQI and health advisories |

### Quick Tips for Interpreting AQI

| AQI Range | Health Impact | Recommended Action |
|-----------|---------------|--------------------|
| 0–50 (Good) | No adverse health effects | Normal outdoor activities |
| 51–100 (Moderate) | Unhealthy for sensitive groups | Reduce prolonged outdoor exertion |
| 101–150 (Unhealthy) | Adverse health effects for everyone | Limit outdoor activity; consider indoor exercise |
| 151–200 (Very Unhealthy) | Serious health effects | Avoid outdoor activity; stay indoors |
| 201+ (Hazardous) | Extremely hazardous | Stay indoors; avoid all outdoor activity |

If you’re planning to be outside in Los Angeles today, it’s a good idea to check one of the above sources before heading out. If you’d like, I can also explain how to interpret specific pollutant readings or suggest ways to reduce exposure.
